0.name: analogy
0.meaning: a structural or thematic resemblance, or a coincidence - no documented relationship

1.name: correlation
1.meaning: shared time, place, presence or sequence - nothing documents that one acted on the other

2.name: contact
2.meaning: documented contact: meetings, correspondence, visits, membership, a shared board

3.name: material
3.meaning: a documented material relationship: ownership, funding, contract, employment, a transfer, a physical link

4.name: coordination
4.meaning: documented joint action: an agreement acted on by both, a joint operation, an instruction

5.name: causation
5.meaning: the record shows A produced B: an official or court finding, or the body's own records

markers.name: MCC New York (closed 2021) - Epstein death site
markers.ctx: Metropolitan Correctional Center, 150 Park Row. Jeffrey Epstein died here 10 Aug 2019 - ruled suicide by hanging (OCME); fracture pattern read as homicide-consistent by family pathologist Michael Baden (attributed, contested). DOJ OIG documented the failure stack: count slips and round sheets falsely certified (no rounds after ~10:40 p.m.), cellmate never replaced against written directive, DVR failed 29 Jul leaving one recording camera that could not see the cell door. The 2025 DOJ 'raw' video was shown by metadata analysis to be assembled in Premiere with ~2m53s absent; later House releases contained the 'missing minute,' contradicting the official explanation. Facility closed 2021. See report Section II - the death record. Sources: OIG 23-085; WIRED; CBS (2025); House Oversight (Sep 2025).

markers.name: FPC Bryan, Texas - Ghislaine Maxwell custody
markers.ctx: Federal Prison Camp Bryan: minimum-security, dormitory-style women's camp. Ghislaine Maxwell - the network's only living convicted principal - was moved here 1 Aug 2025, one week after nine hours of immunized DOJ interviews, despite BOP policy ordinarily excluding sex offenders from camps; officials called the transfer 'highly unusual.' She invoked the Fifth to Congress (Feb 2026) while a pardon stays publicly un-ruled-out; the Senate opposed clemency by unanimous resolution (Jul 2026). Projected release 2037. The documented leverage structure around the surviving node - see report Section V. Sources: BOP; CNN (Aug 2025); Axios (Feb/Jul 2026).

markers.name: Mount of Olives Cemetery, Jerusalem (Robert Maxwell grave)
markers.ctx: Robert Maxwell - Ghislaine's father - buried here 10 Nov 1991 with near-state honors: PM Shamir and President Herzog (eulogy) attended, days after he went overboard from the yacht Lady Ghislaine. The widely repeated 'six intelligence chiefs in attendance' claim traces to secondary literature; the Shamir quote cannot be verified verbatim. The scene itself is the documented signal: a foreign publisher buried on the Mount of Olives with a head of state eulogizing. See report Section V - The Maxwell Template. Sources: JTA (Nov 1991); Times of Israel (2020).

markers.name: Headington Hill Hall, Oxford (Pergamon Press HQ)
markers.ctx: Robert Maxwell's Pergamon Press headquarters and residence. Scientific publishing was a near-perfect Cold War access vehicle: legitimate East-West passage, standing contact with scientists on both sides. Built from contacts made in his 1945-47 press-control posting in British-occupied Berlin. UK DTI verdict (1971): 'not a person who can be relied on to exercise proper stewardship of a publicly quoted company.' Sources: DTI report (1971); Wikipedia (sourced).

markers.name: Lady Ghislaine last position, off Gran Canaria (approx.)
markers.ctx: Robert Maxwell went overboard from his yacht Lady Ghislaine near here, 5 Nov 1991 (position approximate). Spanish inquest: heart attack followed by accidental drowning - no official finding of suicide or murder; both persist as commentary only. Two weeks earlier he had sued Seymour Hersh over The Samson Option's Mossad allegations. The ~£426-460M Mirror pension fraud surfaced within weeks of his death. The record leaves the death readable three ways; no reading is established. Sources: Spanish inquest reporting (Dec 1991); Washington Post (Oct 1991).

markers.name: Axon Enterprise HQ, Scottsdale AZ (approx.)
markers.ctx: Axon Enterprise (Taser) HQ. Acquired Carbyne for $625M; deal closed ~Feb 2026 (Axon took the remaining ~89% stake). Carbyne's NG911 caller-geolocation and live-video capability - the Epstein-funded, Barak-chaired firm - now operates inside a publicly-traded US police-technology company serving ~300 emergency centers across 23 states. BLOWBACK NODE: the surveillance capability consolidated, it did not dissolve. Sources: Axon press release (Nov 2025); GovTech; Forbes (Feb 2026).

markers.name: East 71st Street Townhouse, NYC
markers.ctx: Former Herbert N. Straus mansion, one of the largest private residences in Manhattan. Its use passed to Epstein via Leslie Wexner / L Brands in the 1990s. Named in victim testimony; sold 2021. Appears throughout the House Oversight EFTA email release as Epstein's operational base. Sources: NYT; USVI filings; House Oversight EFTA release. CURRENT OWNER: sold 2021 (~$51M) to a former Goldman Sachs executive.

markers.name: Zorro Ranch, Stanley, New Mexico
markers.ctx: 7,560 deeded acres (plus leased state land), bought 1993, held through Zorro Trust, later Cypress, Inc. Named in victim testimony and New Mexico AG inquiries. Sources: NYT; NM AG. CURRENT OWNER: sold 2023 to the Huffines family (renamed San Rafael Ranch).

markers.name: Little St. James, USVI (LSJ)
markers.ctx: Epstein's private island, central to the trafficking allegations. USVI v. Epstein estate settled for ~$105M (2022). Source: USVI Dept. of Justice. CURRENT OWNER: Little & Great St. James sold ~2023 (~$60M) to Stephen Deckoff (Black Diamond Capital) for a planned resort; half the island's sale proceeds go to the USVI Government under the 2022 settlement, for a trust serving victims of sexual abuse and trafficking.

markers.name: Great St. James, USVI
markers.ctx: Adjacent island Epstein acquired in 2016. Source: USVI filings.

markers.name: El Brillo Way, Palm Beach
markers.ctx: Site of the 2005-06 Palm Beach Police investigation whose federal handling became the 2008 non-prosecution agreement (see Acosta). Sources: Palm Beach PD; DOJ OPR report (2020). STATUS: mansion demolished 2021; the lot was resold — nothing of the original structure remains.

markers.name: Avenue Foch, Paris (Epstein apartment)
markers.ctx: Epstein's Paris apartment, referenced in the French judicial investigation connected to Jean-Luc Brunel. Sources: Paris Prosecutor; OCRVP (judicial police).

markers.name: Carbyne (Reporty) HQ, Tel Aviv
markers.ctx: Israeli-founded NG911 emergency-call-routing / caller-geolocation firm. Epstein was an investor; former Israeli PM Ehud Barak chaired it. A documented Epstein-Barak-surveillance-tech tie and a key node of the HYPOTHESIS layer. Sources: Bloomberg; Haaretz; MintPress. UPDATE (2026): Carbyne was acquired by Axon Enterprise (Taser) for $625M, deal closed ~Feb 2026; Barak exited the board in 2020; later backers include Founders Fund (Peter Thiel) and a 2025 AT&T-led $100M round. Sources: Axon (Nov 2025); GovTech; Forbes (Feb 2026).

markers.name: Apollo Global Management (Leon Black), 9 W 57th St
markers.ctx: Apollo founder Leon Black paid Epstein ~$158M (2012-2017) for tax/estate structuring, per the independent Dechert LLP review (2021); Black later stepped down as Apollo CEO. In-corpus: Epstein family-office threads reference Apollo stock and ~$190M cash. This is established public record (a payment), not an adjudicated crime. Sources: Dechert review (2021); SEC; NYT. UPDATE (2026): a federal securities class action (SDNY, Mar 2026) alleges Apollo/Black concealed Epstein business ties after Feb-2026 file releases; a Delaware derivative suit over exit payments is also ongoing. Litigation unresolved.

markers.name: MIT Media Lab, Cambridge
markers.ctx: Accepted Epstein-linked donations; director Joi Ito resigned in 2019 after reporting (Ronan Farrow, The New Yorker) that the Lab concealed Epstein's gifts. Source: The New Yorker; MIT / Goodwin Procter report (2020).

markers.name: MC2 Model Management (Jean-Luc Brunel), Miami (approx.)
markers.ctx: Modeling agency founded in Miami in 2005 (offices Miami and New York) with a $1M line of credit from Epstein, per its former bookkeeper's deposition (attributed). Brunel was charged in France with rape of minors and died in La Sante prison in Feb 2022. jmail topic tag: 'Conspiring w/ Brunel'. Sources: Paris Prosecutor; AFP.

markers.name: Deutsche Bank (former US HQ, 60 Wall St), NYC
markers.ctx: Epstein's principal bank after JPMorgan exited the relationship (~2013-2018). July 2020: New York Dept. of Financial Services imposed a $150M consent-order penalty for significant compliance failures, expressly including the bank's handling of the Epstein account - a documented, penalty-paid finding, not merely alleged. This is the institutional record; no individual banker is pinned. Sources: NYDFS consent order & press release (7 Jul 2020). UPDATE: an Aug 4 2026 Senate Finance (Wyden) report alleges DB was late filing SARs on >$250M in suspicious Epstein-linked wires - Wyden's finding. DB separately paid $75M to survivors (2023) without admitting liability.

markers.name: Bank of America Tower (One Bryant Park), NYC
markers.ctx: Third bank to settle with Epstein survivors: agreed Mar 2026 to pay ~$72.5M in Doe v. Bank of America (1:25-cv-08520, SDNY; >=60 survivors, period June 2008-July 2019); finally approved 27 Aug 2026 by U.S. District Judge Jed Rakoff. Settlement carries NO admission of liability. Completes the bank cluster after JPMorgan (~$290M, 2023) and Deutsche Bank ($75M victims settlement, 2023). Institutional record; no individual pinned. Sources: American Banker; NBC; court docket 1:25-cv-08520; Barchart.

markers.name: La Sante Prison, Paris (Brunel custody death)
markers.ctx: Jean-Luc Brunel - MC2 modeling agent, charged in France with rape of minors and suspected of procuring for Epstein - was found dead in his cell here, 19 Feb 2022; ruled suicide by hanging. A second charged principal dead in custody before trial, echoing the MCC record two nodes over. (Brunel deceased.) Sources: Paris Prosecutor; AFP; Reuters (Feb 2022).

markers.name: USVI Superior Court, Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas
markers.ctx: Venue of the Epstein estate probate, docket ST-19-PB-80 (~$577M estate). The court appointed Special Master Rosalie Ballentine to account for the estate's assets, liabilities, income and expenditures. Seven reports exist: the first (Sept 2020) is public; reports 3-6 are SEALED. Motions to unseal by the New York Times and McClatchy (Miami Herald) were DENIED three times - 23 Sep 2025, 3 Oct 2025, and reconsideration denied 29 Jan 2026 - on grounds that third-party privacy outweighs access, that the reports are not judicial documents, and that the Epstein Files Transparency Act reaches only DOJ-held material, not the estate's. A court-ordered reconstruction of where the money went exists, and access to it has been litigated and refused. NOTE: online 'forensic' reconstructions claiming $2.1B across shell entities are amateur analyses, not this court's work. Sources: St. Thomas Source (Aug 2025); Virgin Islands Daily News.

markers.name: Edge Foundation / Brockman Inc., NYC (approx.)
markers.ctx: John Brockman's literary agency and the Edge Foundation - the intellectual gatekeeper of Epstein's science network (report Section VI). Epstein-linked foundations supplied roughly 74% of Edge's income 2001-2017 ($638K of $857K), funding the 'billionaires' dinners' that introduced him to Minsky, Pinker, Dawkins, Dennett and others; Edge ended the dinner after his final 2015 donation. Position approximate. Sources: BuzzFeed News (Aldhous, 2019); Slate (Aug 2019).

markers.name: Marshall BioResources - North Rose, NY (HQ)
markers.ctx: Marshall BioResources / Marshall Farms - 5800 Lake Bluff Road, Town of Huron, Wayne County, NY. Founded 1939 (Marshall Farms Group Ltd), privately held. Breeds dogs (beagles), ferrets, cats and minipigs for research. Protesting advocates (Beagle Lovers & Rescuers; Against All Oddz; 3-day protest from 28 May 2026) say it houses some 66,000 animals incl. 20,000+ beagles and cite 20+ Animal Welfare Act citations over the years; the company says USDA inspections in May, June and September 2026 were clean, with no citations. FOLLOW THE MONEY: no public shareholders; revenue is customer sales (pharma/CRO) plus U.S. federal contracts - USAspending (UEI DVGAR51JKM99) direct awards as recorded by the site: ~2.36M, DoD the largest share (unverified re-pull pending). Inference, not a document: NIH-funded research is a larger indirect buyer. Sources: 13WHAM (May 2026); WHEC (Sept 2026); Wikipedia; USAspending.gov.

markers.name: Marshall BioResources - MBR Acres, Wyton, UK
markers.ctx: MBR Acres, Wyton, Cambridgeshire, England. Marshall beagle-breeding facility supplying UK research labs; up to ~2,000 beagles bred per year. Long-running site of the 'Camp Beagle' protest. Part of Marshall's global network.

markers.name: Marshall BioResources - Gannat, France
markers.ctx: Marshall BioResources beagle-breeding site at Gannat, Allier, France - MBR began breeding there in 2017 (per One Voice). Part of Marshall's European breeding network; subject of a 2023 National Assembly written question (no. 11944).

markers.name: Marshall BioResources - Mézilles, France
markers.ctx: Centre d'Élevage du Domaine des Souches, Mézilles, Yonne, France — acquired by Marshall BioResources. Breeds beagles and golden retrievers for laboratories. Part of Marshall's European breeding network.

markers.name: Charles River Laboratories - HQ, Wilmington, MA
markers.ctx: Charles River Laboratories - 251 Ballardvale St, Wilmington, MA. Global contract research organization and breeder of research models incl. beagles. CBS News (Feb 2014): the largest research company using dogs in Massachusetts, with 750 dogs. FOLLOW THE MONEY: publicly traded (NYSE: CRL). Latest Schedule 13G filings: FMR LLC 10.2% (31 Aug 2026), Vanguard Capital Management 7.38% (31 Mar 2026), BlackRock 6.9% (31 Mar 2025), Invesco 6.2% (30 Jun 2026); Wellington 3.6% (31 Dec 2025, below the 5% line). Much of it index ownership. Sources: SEC 13G/13G-A; CRL 10-K FY2025; CBS News (2014).

markers.name: Charles River - Stone Ridge, NY (breeding, approx.)
markers.ctx: Charles River breeding facility, Stone Ridge (Town of Marbletown), Ulster County, NY (RR 209). Long-documented dog/beagle breeding site. Pin at town level — exact parcel pending. Source: SourceWatch.

markers.name: Inotiv - HQ, West Lafayette, IN
markers.ctx: Inotiv, Inc. (formerly Bioanalytical Systems, BASi) - 2701 Kent Ave, West Lafayette, IN. Parent of Envigo RMS. Emerged from prepackaged Chapter 11 on 19 July 2026; delisted from Nasdaq and SEC registration terminated (July 2026). Sources: Inotiv 8-K filings (June-July 2026); Wikipedia.

markers.name: Envigo / Inotiv - Cumberland, VA (approx.)
markers.ctx: Envigo RMS beagle-breeding facility, Cumberland County, VA. ~4,000 beagles relinquished to the Humane Society under a July 2022 settlement. 3 June 2024: Envigo RMS pleaded guilty to conspiring to violate the Animal Welfare Act and Envigo Global Services to a Clean Water Act conspiracy; parent Inotiv guaranteed more than $35M - the largest fine ever in an AWA case (DOJ/EPA). FOLLOW THE MONEY: Inotiv filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 on 3 June 2026 (Bankruptcy Court, S.D. Texas) under a 2 June 2026 restructuring support agreement: a $65.4M DIP from the consenting first-lien lenders ($25M new money + $40.4M roll-up), ~$326M of funded debt converted to equity; first-lien lenders take 93% of new equity, second-lien PIK and convertible noteholders share 7% plus warrants; DOJ plea claims reinstated; existing shares cancelled. Emerged 19 July 2026. The filings name creditor classes, not funds. Pin at county level - exact parcel pending. Sources: EPA/DOJ (June 2024); Inotiv 8-Ks (June-July 2026).

markers.name: The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) - Bar Harbor, ME
markers.ctx: The Jackson Laboratory - 600 Main St, Bar Harbor, Maine. Nonprofit (founded 1929); one of the world's largest suppliers of laboratory mice (13,000+ strains, 'JAX Mice', per JAX). Additional sites: Farmington CT, Sacramento CA, Shanghai (China) and Yokohama (Japan). Source: JAX; Wikipedia.

markers.name: Taconic Biosciences - HQ, Rensselaer, NY
markers.ctx: Taconic Biosciences HQ, 1 Discovery Drive, Rensselaer, NY 12144 (Albany Health Sciences Campus). Major rodent-model breeder: 3 service labs + 6 breeding facilities across the U.S. and Europe (incl. Germany, Denmark); primary U.S. breeding operations ~45 mi south in Germantown, NY. Source: Taconic; Discover Rensselaer.

markers.name: Janvier Labs - Le Genest-Saint-Isle, France
markers.ctx: Janvier Labs - Le Genest-Saint-Isle, Mayenne, France. Breeder of research rodents (mice/rats), founded 1960. Source: Janvier Labs.

markers.name: GemPharmatech - Nanjing, China (approx.)
markers.ctx: GemPharmatech - Nanjing, Jiangsu, China (pin at city level). Founded 2017; mouse-model breeder (knockout/humanized strains), self-described as Asia's largest provider of laboratory mouse models. Opened an expanded U.S. headquarters and vivarium in San Diego, CA (April 2025). Source: GemPharmatech; Newswise (17 Apr 2025).

markers.name: Charles River - Vital River, Beijing, China (approx.)
markers.ctx: Beijing Vital River Laboratory Animal Technology - Charles River's China rodent-breeding arm; CRL bought the remaining 8% equity in fiscal 2025, making it wholly owned. Pin at city level. Source: Charles River 10-K FY2025.

markers.name: Hylasco Bio-Technology (Charles River licensee), Hyderabad, India (approx.)
markers.ctx: Hylasco Bio-Technology, Hyderabad - breeds SPF rats and mice under licence from Charles River (partnership announced 2016) and imports CRL models; a licensee, not a CRL subsidiary. Pin at city level. Source: Hylasco; Lab Animal (Nature).

markers.name: Charles River - Kuopio, Finland
markers.ctx: Charles River Discovery Services, Kuopio, Finland - neuroscience-focused non-GLP pharmacology site (founded as Cerebricon 2001, acquired by CRL 2009) with small-animal imaging; moved to a new purpose-built facility in 2025 (+40% space). Source: Charles River (28 Feb 2025).

markers.name: Vanny Bio-Research - Pursat Province, Cambodia (approx.)
markers.ctx: Vanny Bio-Research macaque farm, Pursat Province, Cambodia (40 ha site opened 2006, per Mongabay). Named in a U.S. federal indictment unsealed Nov 2022 (S.D. Florida) alleging that up to 3,000 wild long-tailed macaques were laundered through Vanny facilities since Dec 2017 with permits falsely declaring them captive-bred; eight defendants charged including two Cambodian Forestry Administration officials. The one official tried, Masphal Kry, was acquitted of all charges (March 2024). Pin at province level. Sources: Mongabay (Nov 2022); RFA (Apr 2024).

markers.name: Noveprim - Mauritius (Charles River 90%)
markers.ctx: Noveprim Group, Mauritius - long-tailed macaque (NHP) supplier. Charles River bought 49% in 2022 and an additional 41% on 30 Nov 2023, giving it a 90% controlling interest. Advocacy groups (PETA, Species Unite) allege, from undercover footage, wild capture of macaques before export. Source: CRL 10-K FY2023; PETA; Species Unite.

markers.name: Bioculture - Rivière des Anguilles, Mauritius
markers.ctx: Bioculture (Mauritius) Ltd, Riviere des Anguilles - founding company of the Bioculture Group; breeds and exports SPF long-tailed (cynomolgus) macaques for biomedical research (since 1985 per the company). Part of the Mauritius primate-export node of the lab-monkey supply chain. Source: Bioculture Group.

markers.name: Microsoft Project Natick - off Orkney, Scotland
markers.ctx: Project Natick - Microsoft's experimental underwater data center. The Phase 2 vessel was placed on the seabed off Orkney (European Marine Energy Centre site) on 1 June 2018 and retrieved in July 2020; the first prototype ran off California in 2015. Microsoft said in 2024 the project was no longer active. Offshore point (approx). Source: Wikipedia, Project Natick; Microsoft.

markers.name: Highlander Hainan Underwater Data Center, China
markers.ctx: Subsea data-center cluster off Lingshui/Sanya, Hainan, China, operated by Highlander (2023). The operator and Chinese state media describe it as the first commercial subsea data center; tonnage and capacity figures (about 1,433 tons; about 60,000 conventional computers) are the operator's. Offshore point (approx). Source: DCD; E&T; Data Center Frontier.

markers.name: Shanghai Offshore Underwater Data Center, China
markers.ctx: Offshore wind-powered underwater data center off the Shanghai coast (Lingang), announced 2025, about 24 MW planned per the developer, which describes it as the first of its kind. Offshore point (approx). Source: Data Center Frontier (2025).

markers.name: Nautilus Data Technologies (floating) - Stockton, CA
markers.ctx: Barge-mounted floating data center (Nautilus Data Technologies) in the Stockton Deep Water Channel, Port of Stockton, California - equipment cooled by circulating channel water returned slightly warmer. Source: Wikipedia, Nautilus Data Technologies; The Record (Stockton), 2016.

markers.name: Keppel Floating Data Center Park - Singapore
markers.ctx: Keppel's nearshore floating data center park concept, Singapore — offshore siting to bypass land/power constraints. Offshore point (approx). Source: Keppel; industry reports.

markers.name: NSA Utah Data Center - Bluffdale, UT
markers.ctx: Intelligence Community Comprehensive National Cybersecurity Initiative Data Center - the NSA-led data storage facility at Camp Williams near Bluffdale, Utah (1 to 1.5 million sq ft; completed May 2014, about $1.5 billion). Central to the post-Snowden bulk-surveillance debate; its precise mission is classified. Source: Wikipedia, Utah Data Center.

markers.name: Ashburn 'Data Center Alley' - Loudoun County, VA
markers.ctx: Ashburn/Loudoun County, Virginia ('Data Center Alley') - the largest concentration of data-center capacity in the United States. Source: Synergy Research; Data Center Frontier (figures not reproduced here pending a read of the primary).

markers.name: Switch Citadel Campus - Tahoe Reno, NV
markers.ctx: Switch 'Citadel' campus, Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada - over 1,000 acres, planned to exceed 7.2 million sq ft of data-center space at completion; the first building (TAHOE RENO 1) opened February 2017. Source: Wikipedia, Switch (company); Data Center Frontier.

markers.name: Stargate AI Campus - Abilene, TX
markers.ctx: Stargate AI data-center campus at Abilene, Texas - the first site of the Stargate joint venture (SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, MGX; announced 21 Jan 2025), developed by Crusoe with Blue Owl and Primary Digital Infrastructure. Pin at city level. Source: Wikipedia, Stargate LLC; Data Center Frontier (2025).

markers.name: Google Data Center - The Dalles, OR
markers.ctx: Google's flagship Columbia River data center, The Dalles, Oregon (since 2006) — hydro-powered. Source: Google; Synergy Research.

markers.name: Meta Data Center - Prineville, OR
markers.ctx: Meta (Facebook) Prineville, Oregon campus - the company's first self-built data center (opened 2011); Apple also operates a data center in Prineville. Source: Meta; industry reports.

markers.name: Google Data Center - Council Bluffs, IA
markers.ctx: Google Council Bluffs, Iowa - announced 2007, first phase completed 2009, expanded 2012 and 2015; one of Google's largest US campuses. Source: Wikipedia, Google data centers.

markers.name: Meta Data Center - Luleå, Sweden
markers.ctx: Meta (Facebook) Luleå data center, Sweden, near the Arctic Circle - announced 27 Oct 2011 as the company's first data center outside the United States; free-air cooling and hydro power. Source: Wikipedia, Luleå; Meta.

markers.name: Google Data Center - Hamina, Finland
markers.ctx: Google Hamina, Finland - built in the former Stora Enso Summa paper mill, bought in 2009; seawater-cooled from the Gulf of Finland; first phase completed 2011. Source: Wikipedia, Google data centers; Google.

markers.name: Ulanqab / Hohhot Hyperscale Corridor, Inner Mongolia
markers.ctx: Ulanqab-Hohhot corridor, Inner Mongolia - a major Chinese hyperscale cluster (China Mobile, Alibaba, ByteDance, Baidu, Tencent, China Telecom among reported operators) within Beijing's 'East Data, West Computing' programme. Capacity figures pending a primary. Source: Data Center Frontier; Synergy Research.

markers.name: Lefdal Mine Datacenter - Nordfjord, Norway
markers.ctx: Data center inside the former Lefdal olivine mine, Nordfjord, Norway — fjord-water cooled, hydro-powered, deep underground. Source: Lefdal Mine; industry reports. Pin approximate.

markers.name: xAI Colossus - Memphis, TN
markers.ctx: xAI 'Colossus' AI supercomputer, south Memphis, Tennessee - built in 122 days, live 2024; xAI claimed expansion toward 2 GW and about 555,000 NVIDIA GPUs (Jan 2026), while independent accounts put the combined sites at about 1 GW by mid-2026. Temporary gas turbines drew local opposition and regulatory scrutiny. Pin at city level. Source: Wikipedia, Colossus (supercomputer); Epoch AI (2026).

markers.name: Meta Hyperion AI Campus - Richland Parish, LA
markers.ctx: Meta 'Hyperion' — a city-sized AI data center in Richland Parish, Louisiana; Zuckerberg says it will scale to ~5 GW over several years. Source: Meta; Data Center Frontier (2025-26).

markers.name: Meta Prometheus AI Campus - New Albany, OH
markers.ctx: Meta 'Prometheus' AI campus, New Albany, Ohio — GW-scale, ~562 MW IT power projected. Source: Epoch AI; Data Center Frontier (2026).

markers.name: Amazon / Anthropic AI Campus - New Carlisle, IN
markers.ctx: Amazon Web Services campus at New Carlisle, Indiana (Project Rainier) — ~1+ GW, built to train Anthropic's models. Source: Epoch AI; AWS (2026).

markers.name: Microsoft Fairwater AI DC - Lithia Springs, GA
markers.ctx: Microsoft 'Fairwater' AI data center, Atlanta area (Lithia Springs), Georgia — ~636 MW. Source: Epoch AI; Microsoft (2025-26).

markers.name: Microsoft Data Center - Boydton, VA
markers.ctx: Microsoft hyperscale cloud campus, Boydton, Virginia (construction began 2010, about $500 million; expanded 2014) - in a town of about 300 people (2020 census). Source: Wikipedia, Boydton, Virginia; Data Center Frontier.

markers.name: Microsoft Data Center - Quincy, WA
markers.ctx: Microsoft Columbia Basin campus, Quincy, Washington — cool climate + cheap hydro; one of the original hyperscale clusters (also Yahoo, Sabey, Dell). Source: Data Center Frontier.

markers.name: Apple iCloud Data Center - Maiden, NC
markers.ctx: Apple iCloud data center, Maiden, Catawba County, North Carolina (about 500,000 sq ft); in May 2012 Apple said it would generate 60 percent of the site's power itself with fuel cells and solar. Google's North Carolina data center is separate, in Lenoir. Source: Wikipedia, Maiden, North Carolina; Google data centers.

markers.name: Pionen 'White Mountains' Bunker DC - Stockholm
markers.ctx: Bahnhof's 'Pionen' data center inside a Cold War nuclear bunker under Vita Bergen park, Södermalm, Stockholm — 30m below granite; once hosted WikiLeaks servers. Source: Bahnhof; public reporting.

markers.name: Alibaba Zhangbei Cloud Campus - Hebei, China
markers.ctx: Alibaba Cloud's Zhangbei (Cloud Valley) hyperscale campus, Hebei, China — cold-climate northern-China node serving Beijing. Source: Alibaba; industry reports.

markers.name: Gui'an Big Data Valley - Guizhou, China
markers.ctx: Gui'an New Area, Guizhou — China's flagship 'big data valley': Apple's China iCloud (via GCBD), Tencent, Huawei, and China Telecom operate mountain/cave-cooled data centers here. Apple's China user data is stored on GCBD-operated servers. Source: public reporting.

markers.name: GDS Hyperscale Campus - Langfang, Hebei, China
markers.ctx: GDS Holdings hyperscale data-center campus, Langfang, Hebei — a core node in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei cloud cluster. Source: GDS filings; industry reports.

markers.name: Green Mountain DC1 - Rennesøy (Stavanger), Norway
markers.ctx: Green Mountain DC1-Stavanger — a Tier III data center built inside a former high-security NATO ammunition store dug into a mountain on Rennesøy, Norway; fjord-water cooled, hydro-powered, ~22,600 m². Source: Green Mountain; Data Centre Magazine.

markers.name: Iron Mountain WPA-1 - Boyers, PA
markers.ctx: Iron Mountain's underground data center in a former limestone mine ~220 ft below Boyers, Pennsylvania — also stores U.S. federal records (OPM retirement archive) and film masters. Source: Iron Mountain; Data Center Knowledge.

markers.name: Swiss Fort Knox - Saanen, Switzerland
markers.ctx: Swiss Fort Knox — a high-security data center inside a former military bunker in the Swiss Alps near Saanen; blast doors, groundwater cooling, redundant hidden entrances. Source: Data Centre Magazine; industry reports.

markers.name: Google AI Campus - West Memphis, AR
markers.ctx: Alphabet/Google broke ground on a data-center campus in West Memphis, Arkansas — directly across the Mississippi from xAI's Colossus in Memphis. Two rival AI megacampuses facing each other across the river. Source: Data Center Frontier (2025).

markers.name: G42 / Stargate UAE - Masdar City, Abu Dhabi
markers.ctx: G42-anchored 'Stargate UAE' AI compute cluster near Masdar City, Abu Dhabi — a sovereign-scale AI data center (OpenAI/Oracle/Nvidia-linked), part of a planned 5 GW campus. Source: Data Center Frontier; company announcements (2025).

markers.name: Google Data Center - St. Ghislain, Belgium
markers.ctx: Google's St. Ghislain, Belgium data center — one of its largest European sites; among the first to run without chillers (free-air/water cooling). Source: Google.

markers.name: Meta Data Center - Clonee, Ireland
markers.ctx: Meta's Clonee, County Meath, Ireland campus — a flagship European hyperscale site; part of Ireland's dense data-center cluster around Dublin. Source: Meta.

markers.name: Subsea Cloud pods - Port Angeles, WA
markers.ctx: Subsea Cloud — commercial subsea data-center pods ('Jules Verne' etc.) designed for seabed deployment; U.S. Pacific Northwest / Gulf of Mexico siting. Offshore point (approx). Source: Subsea Cloud; Data Center Frontier.

markers.name: Vanguard Group - Malvern, PA
markers.ctx: The Vanguard Group, Malvern, PA. Its affiliate Vanguard Capital Management reported 3,634,376 Charles River Laboratories shares (7.38%) as of 31 Mar 2026 (Schedule 13G), after a January 2026 internal realignment moved the holding out of The Vanguard Group, Inc. Second to FMR (10.2%, Aug 2026) among disclosed holders. Predominantly index funds. Source: SEC Schedule 13G / 13G-A.

markers.name: BlackRock - 50 Hudson Yards, NYC
markers.ctx: BlackRock, Inc., 50 Hudson Yards, New York. Reported 6.9% of Charles River Laboratories (Schedule 13G/A, 31 Mar 2025). World's largest asset manager by AUM. Source: SEC 13G/A; CRL proxy 2026.

markers.name: State Street - 1 Congress St, Boston
markers.ctx: State Street Corp, Boston. Top-tier institutional holder of Charles River Laboratories (the third of the 'Big Three' index managers). Source: Fintel/13F.

markers.name: FMR / Fidelity - 245 Summer St, Boston
markers.ctx: FMR LLC (Fidelity), 245 Summer St, Boston. Largest disclosed holder of Charles River Laboratories: 4,865,628 shares, 10.2%, as of 31 Aug 2026 (Schedule 13G/A filed 8 Sept 2026). Source: SEC 13G/A.

markers.name: Wellington Management - Boston
markers.ctx: Wellington Management Group LLP, Boston. Held 1,749,213 Charles River Laboratories shares (3.6%) as of 31 Dec 2025 - below the 5% reporting line after a prior larger stake. Source: SEC 13G/A (Feb 2026).

markers.name: U.S. Dept of Defense / DHA - Falls Church, VA
markers.ctx: U.S. Department of Defense — Marshall BioResources' largest federal buyer: ~1.84M in direct awards (USAspending, all years), largely DoD military-medical research (e.g. USUHS). Node at Defense Health Agency HQ. Source: USAspending.gov.

markers.name: NIH / HHS - Bethesda, MD
markers.ctx: National Institutes of Health / Dept of Health & Human Services, Bethesda, MD. ~415K in direct awards to Marshall BioResources per USAspending (as recorded by the site; re-pull pending). Inference, not a document: NIH grants fund much of the university research that buys from these breeders. Source: USAspending.gov; NIH RePORTER.

markers.name: Bank for International Settlements (BIS)
markers.ctx: Constituted 27 Feb 1930, opened in Basel 17 May 1930. Owned by 63 central banks (bis.org). March 1939: transferred 23 tons of gold held for Czechoslovakia to the Reichsbank. Bretton Woods (1944) recommended its liquidation; the decision was reversed in 1948. Private shareholders were bought out from 2001.

markers.name: Basel, Switzerland
markers.ctx: Seat of the Bank for International Settlements, which serves as a bank for central banks and is owned by 63 of them.

markers.name: Jekyll Island, Georgia
markers.ctx: 20-30 November 1910: six men - Senator Nelson Aldrich, A. Piatt Andrew, Henry Davison, Arthur Shelton, Frank Vanderlip and Paul Warburg - met in secret at the Jekyll Island Club to draft a banking-reform plan that laid a foundation for the Federal Reserve. Participants did not admit the meeting until the 1930s.

markers.name: Federal Reserve, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: Federal Reserve Act signed by President Wilson 23 Dec 1913, the day the Senate passed it 43-25 (House 298-60 on 22 Dec). A presidentially appointed Board of Governors over 12 regional Reserve Banks; member banks must hold Reserve Bank stock, which cannot be transferred (12 U.S.C. 287).

markers.name: JP Morgan HQ, New York
markers.ctx: JPMorgan Chase headquarters, 270 Park Avenue. Its predecessor J.P. Morgan & Co.: a Jekyll Island Club member, most likely J.P. Morgan, arranged the club for the 1910 meeting (Federal Reserve History). Alan Greenspan was a J.P. Morgan & Co. director before chairing the Fed (1987-2006).

markers.name: Kuhn, Loeb & Co., New York
markers.ctx: Investment bank, 1867-1977 (merged into Lehman Brothers). Paul Warburg, a partner from 1902, attended the 1910 Jekyll Island meeting, advocated central banking, and sat on the original Federal Reserve Board 1914-1918 (vice chairman 1916-18). Died 1932.

markers.name: Chase Manhattan / Rockefeller, New York
markers.ctx: Chase Manhattan Bank, chaired by David Rockefeller 1969-81. Paul Volcker moved between it and government: NY Fed economist (1952), Chase (1957), Treasury (1962), Chase (1965), Treasury (1969), NY Fed president (1975), Fed Chair (1979-87).

markers.name: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR), New York
markers.ctx: Founded 1921. Harold Pratt House, 58 East 68th Street. About 5,400 members (2025); membership has included secretaries of state and CIA directors. Chaired by David Rubenstein since 2017.

markers.name: Bilderberg Hotel, Oosterbeek, Netherlands
markers.ctx: First Bilderberg Meeting, 29-31 May 1954, at this hotel. Annual meetings of about 150 invited politicians, bankers, executives and journalists, held under the Chatham House Rule.

markers.name: Trilateral Commission (founded New York, 1973)
markers.ctx: Founded July 1973 by David Rockefeller and Zbigniew Brzezinski. Published The Crisis of Democracy (1975; Crozier, Huntington, Watanuki) on the governability of democracies. North American Group now based in Washington D.C.

markers.name: Vatican City - St. Peter's Square
markers.ctx: Independent city-state since the Lateran Treaty, 11 Feb 1929; elective absolute monarchy; seat of a church of about 1.3 billion baptised Catholics. The obelisk came from Heliopolis (per Pliny) via Alexandria; Caligula shipped it to Rome c. 40 AD.

markers.name: City of London Corporation (Square Mile)
markers.ctx: Local authority of the Square Mile; first recorded royal charter c.1067 (William I). Own police force and Lord Mayor. Business voters (about 24,000 in 2009) greatly outnumber resident voters.

markers.name: Cleopatra's Needle, Victoria Embankment, London
markers.ctx: Egyptian obelisk from Heliopolis (1450 BC, Pharaoh Thutmose III). Brought to London 1878. Same origin as Vatican obelisk.

markers.name: Washington Monument, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: 555 ft 5.125 in. Egyptian obelisk design - NPS: 'evoking timelessness of ancient civilizations'. Aluminum cap inscribed 'Laus Deo'. Masonic cornerstone July 4, 1848.

markers.name: Place de la Concorde Obelisk, Paris
markers.ctx: Obelisk of Luxor: one of a pair carved for the portal of Luxor Temple under Ramesses II (c.1250 BC); its twin still stands at Luxor. Not part of the London-New York pair, which came from Heliopolis via Alexandria.

markers.name: Cleopatra's Needle, Central Park, New York
markers.ctx: Erected at Heliopolis under Thutmose III (c.1475 BC), later moved to Alexandria; installed in Central Park 22 Feb 1881. Twin of the London Cleopatra's Needle.

markers.name: East India Company, London
markers.ctx: Chartered 31 Dec 1600, dissolved 1 June 1874. Its presidency armies reached about 260,000 soldiers, at times twice the British Army; it ran courts and minted coin. The report reads it as a prototype of corporate sovereignty.

markers.name: M. M. Warburg & Co., Hamburg
markers.ctx: Private bank founded 1798, headquartered on Ferdinandstrasse. Max Warburg directed it 1910-1938, when Nazi Aryanisation forced him out; he emigrated to New York (died 1946). His brother Paul moved to Kuhn, Loeb in New York in 1902 and died in 1932.

markers.name: Citadel (founded Chicago 1990; HQ Miami since 2022)
markers.ctx: Ken Griffin's hedge fund, founded in Chicago 1990; headquarters moved to Miami in 2022. Ben Bernanke, Fed Chair 2006-14 through the 2008 crisis, became a Citadel senior adviser in April 2015.

markers.name: Carlyle Group, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: Private equity firm, HQ 1001 Pennsylvania Avenue NW. Fed Chair Jerome Powell was a Carlyle partner 1997-2005. Co-founder David Rubenstein has chaired the Council on Foreign Relations since 2017.

markers.name: General Dynamics HQ, Reston, VA
markers.ctx: HQ Reston. 1959: Henry Crown merged Material Service Corp. into GD and became its largest shareholder. Only U.S. maker of MK-80 series bomb bodies, reported as the main bomb type in Israel's Gaza campaign. Sold its Electronics Division to the Carlyle Group in 1992.

markers.name: Aspen Institute, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: Think tank founded 1949; Washington HQ at 2300 N Street NW. Runs the Henry Crown Fellowship (est. 1997), named for the Chicago industrialist who became General Dynamics' largest shareholder in 1959.

markers.name: ADL Headquarters, New York
markers.ctx: Anti-Defamation League, founded 1913; headquarters in Murray Hill, Manhattan. CEO Jonathan Greenblatt.

markers.name: Harvard Law School, Cambridge, MA
markers.ctx: Dershowitz joined the Harvard Law faculty in 1964; full professor in 1967 at 28, then the youngest in the school's history; Felix Frankfurter Professor of Law from 1993; retired 2013.

markers.name: Palm Beach County, FL - Epstein NPA
markers.ctx: Dershowitz was on Epstein's defence team and helped negotiate the non-prosecution agreement approved by U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta (signed 2007). It granted immunity to Epstein, four named co-conspirators and any unnamed 'potential co-conspirators'; victims were not told. Judge Kenneth Marra ruled in 2019 that it violated the Crime Victims' Rights Act; the 11th Circuit reversed in 2020.

markers.name: New Jersey Turnpike - Nash Crash Site
markers.ctx: May 23, 2015: John Nash and wife Alicia killed in taxi crash returning from Norway (Abel Prize). Nash proposed 'Ideal Money' - a currency standard pegged to an industrial consumption price index; reading it as a description of Bitcoin is later commentary, not his claim. Both ejected - not wearing seatbelts.

markers.name: Temple City, California - Hal Finney
markers.ctx: Hal Finney lived here for about ten years, a few blocks from Dorian Satoshi Nakamoto (Forbes, 2014). Received first Bitcoin transaction from Satoshi (2009). Created first reusable proof-of-work system (RPOW). Finney died 28 Aug 2014 (ALS).

markers.name: Alcor, Scottsdale, Arizona
markers.ctx: Alcor Life Extension Foundation. Finney's body cryopreserved at -196°C. Bitcoin's first transaction recipient is stored in a desert facility. Peter Thiel also reportedly signed up for cryopreservation.

markers.name: Cheyenne Mountain, Colorado
markers.ctx: NORAD/USNORTHCOM alternate command center under ~2,000 ft of granite; ~5.1 acres. Built 1961-66, operational 1966. 2015: $700M Raytheon contract to move communications systems into the EMP-hardened complex (Adm. Gortney).

markers.name: Raven Rock (Site R), Pennsylvania
markers.ctx: Alternate National Military Command Center (Site R). Built 1951-53. About 6 miles from Camp David; an underground link between the two is rumoured, not documented.

markers.name: Camp David, Maryland
markers.ctx: Presidential retreat on Catoctin Mountain. Raven Rock (Site R), the alternate military command center, lies about 6 miles away; an underground corridor between them is rumoured, not documented.

markers.name: Mount Weather, Bluemont, Virginia
markers.ctx: Emergency Operations Center. FEMA High Point Special Facility. Classified continuity-of-government facility.

markers.name: The Greenbrier, White Sulphur Springs, WV
markers.ctx: Project Greek Island - secret Congressional bunker built 1958-61 beneath luxury resort. Decommissioned 1992 after media exposure.

markers.name: Mount Yamantau, Urals, Russia
markers.ctx: Large excavation observed by U.S. satellite imagery into the late 1990s; purpose never disclosed. Russia (1996) declined to inform foreign media about 'facilities under construction'. A 1997 U.S. Congressional finding cited a 'deception and denial policy'. Closed town of Mezhgorye (formed 1995 from Beloretsk-15 and -16) serves the site.

markers.name: Kosvinsky Kamen, Urals, Russia
markers.ctx: Command-post bunker under ~300 m of granite (Jane's, 1994). U.S. analysts believe it houses the command post of Perimeter ('Dead Hand'), a semi-automatic retaliation system; accounts differ on whether launch still needs human approval once activated.

markers.name: Moscow - Metro-2 / D-6
markers.ctx: Officially unacknowledged deep metro, said to link the Kremlin, FSB headquarters, Vnukovo-2 government airport and an underground town at Ramenki. Russia has never confirmed it.

markers.name: Project 131, Hubei Province, China
markers.ctx: Underground Project 131: military command headquarters tunnelled under a hill at Gaoqiao, Xianning, Hubei (~80 km south of Wuhan), decided 31 January 1969 (hence '131'), with offices for Mao Zedong and Lin Biao. Now a tourist site.

markers.name: Beijing Underground City
markers.ctx: Civil-defence tunnel network built 1969-79 on Mao's order during the Sino-Soviet border crisis, dug by more than 300,000 local citizens; the plan was to move half of Beijing's population underground.

markers.name: 816 Nuclear Military Plant, Chongqing, China
markers.ctx: Underground plutonium-production complex near Fuling, Chongqing, begun 1966 (Third Front) by more than 60,000 PLA engineering soldiers; cancelled February 1984 when nearly complete and never operated. Declassified 2002; opened to tourists 2010.

markers.name: Burlington / Corsham, Wiltshire, UK
markers.ctx: Central Government War Headquarters: 35-acre complex ~120 ft underground in former Corsham stone quarries, for up to 4,000 officials. Decommissioned December 2004.

markers.name: Jerusalem Underground Command, Israel
markers.ctx: Crisis command center beneath the Judaean Mountains. Israeli continuity-of-government facility.

markers.name: Klara Bunker, Stockholm, Sweden
markers.ctx: Capacity 8,000-12,000 people. Sweden has 65,000+ fallout shelters for 10 million population.

markers.name: Svalbard Global Seed Vault, Arctic Norway
markers.ctx: Opened 26 February 2008. Built, owned and fully funded by the Government of Norway; run by NordGen with the Crop Trust part-funding operations. Seeds are held under 'black box' terms: boxes are never opened and only the depositing genebank can withdraw them. First withdrawal: ICARDA, 2015-2019, to rebuild a collection lost to the Syrian war. 1.4 million+ samples from 134 institutions (2026).

markers.name: Diefenbunker, Ottawa, Canada
markers.ctx: CFS Carp Emergency Government Headquarters, built 1959-61. Now Diefenbunker: Canada's Cold War Museum.

markers.name: COFAS, Taverny, France
markers.ctx: Headquarters of the Strategic Air Forces Command (France's air-launched nuclear force) 1964-2007 and again since 2024, with a hardened command centre 70-80 m below ground in a former gypsum quarry.

markers.name: Mont Verdun, near Lyon, France
markers.ctx: Air Base 942 Lyon-Mont Verdun: air defence and operations centre (CDAOA South sector, linked to NATO ACCS) with an underground alternate strategic command centre hardened against chemical and nuclear attack.

markers.name: Regierungsbunker, Ahrweiler, Germany
markers.ctx: Federal government emergency bunker built 1960-72 in disused railway tunnels of the Ahr valley; 17.3 km of tunnels. Decommissioned 1997; a short section is now the Government Bunker Documentation Site, the rest abandoned and sealed.

markers.name: K-116, Zlíchov, Prague, Czech Republic
markers.ctx: Cold War-era underground command bunker beneath Zlíchov hill. Eastern Bloc continuity infrastructure.

markers.name: REGAN Vest, Jutland, Denmark
markers.ctx: REGAN Vest: Denmark's Cold War civil-government nuclear bunker in Rold Skov forest, northern Jutland.

markers.name: Salt Pit / 'The Dark Prison', North Kabul, Afghanistan
markers.ctx: CIA facility. Detainee Gul Rahman froze to death November 2002. 'Enhanced interrogation' - the U.S. government's euphemism for torture.

markers.name: Stare Kiejkuty, Poland
markers.ctx: Former intelligence facility converted to CIA black site. Confirmed by European Court of Human Rights 2014.

markers.name: Detention Site Black, Bucharest, Romania
markers.ctx: ECHR, Al Nashiri v. Romania (31 May 2018): Romania hosted a CIA secret prison, 'Detention Site Black', Sept 2003 - Nov 2005, and was complicit in the ill-treatment held there. The 2014 Senate report places Al Nashiri in Bucharest. Exact building not established here; Mihail Kogălniceanu airbase was a reported flight point, not the established detention site.

markers.name: Antaviliai, Lithuania
markers.ctx: Former riding school converted to CIA detention facility. Confirmed ECHR 2018. Another EU/NATO state hosting black sites.

markers.name: Ramasun Station / 'Detention Site Green', Thailand
markers.ctx: Former U.S. Army Security Agency intercept station (7th RRFS, built 1964). Suspected by some as the CIA's first black site, 'Detention Site Green' (Abu Zubaydah, March 2002); a senior Thai official instead placed that site at Udorn RTAFB, and the Royal Thai Army denies Ramasun's use. Location contested.

markers.name: Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti
markers.ctx: U.S. base leased from Djibouti in 2002; supports CIA and DoD counter-terrorism and drone operations in Yemen and Somalia. Djibouti is listed among states reported to have assisted CIA rendition (attributed).

markers.name: Diego Garcia, British Indian Ocean Territory
markers.ctx: UK territory leased to the U.S. The UK admitted (Feb 2008) that two U.S. rendition flights refuelled here in 2002; detention on the island is alleged, not established. Chagossians expelled 1968-1973 to make way for the base. 2025 treaty transfers sovereignty to Mauritius, base retained for 99 years.

markers.name: Negev Nuclear Research Center, Dimona, Israel
markers.ctx: Dimona reactor, ~13 km SE of Dimona; built in secret outside IAEA inspection. U.S. inspections ran 1965-69 with advance notice; Israel reportedly installed temporary false walls before each, and the inspectors reportedly told Washington the visits were useless (attributed).

markers.name: Little Saint James Island, U.S. Virgin Islands
markers.ctx: 70-78 acres. A 2005 power and fibre-optic cable from St Thomas gave the island dedicated connections; a maintenance building has sally-port doors. Sold May 2023, with Great Saint James, to Stephen Deckoff's SD Investments for US$60 million; announced plan: a luxury resort.

markers.name: The Octagon (State Strategic Command Center) - New Capital, Egypt
markers.ctx: Egypt's Ministry of Defence headquarters, inaugurated July 2026. Official name: State Strategic Command Center. 22,000 acres (89 km²) across 13 zones, ~1,160 acres of floor area, eight buildings set around a ring; the Pentagon is one building of about 29 acres. Sits inside the New Capital, 45 km east of Cairo, whose governing vehicle ACUD is 51% Ministry of Defence, alongside 6,000+ AI cameras and the Iconic Tower (393.8m). Who financed the complex is not in the public record: US FMF ($1.3bn/yr since 1987) is disbursed to US contractors from a Federal Reserve Bank of New York account and cannot buy Egyptian construction; CSCEC financing is documented for the CBD, not for this; no Israeli funding is documented at any tier — Israeli coverage of the Octagon is the worried kind.

markers.name: Tura–Masara limestone quarries, Egypt
markers.ctx: About 6 km of underground limestone galleries on the Nile's east bank, ~12 km south of Cairo and west of the Octagon. Cut as tunnels, not open pits, with limestone pillars left standing to carry the roofs. Source of the Great Pyramid's outer casing (~67,390 m³ of fine Tura limestone for Khufu alone). Mapped for the British military in WWII for use as bomb-proof storage. Now the Tura cement works — Portland and oil-well cement — under Heidelberg Materials. Three tenancies in one hole in the ground; continuity of use is not continuity of purpose.

markers.name: NEOM / THE LINE, Saudi Arabia
markers.ctx: Announced 2021 as a 170 km linear city, 200 m wide and 500 m tall; by 2024 a first phase of 2.4 km was reported (WSJ/Bloomberg; Saudi officials denied) and by 2025 the project was substantially scaled down or suspended. OXAGON industrial port; TROJENA ski resort (lost the 2029 Asian Winter Games to Kazakhstan, 2026). April 2020: Howeitat tribesman Abdul Rahim al-Huwaiti, who refused eviction, was shot dead by Saudi security forces (who said he opened fire; disputed); three other tribe members were later sentenced to death.

markers.name: Songdo International Business District, South Korea
markers.ctx: Built on 1,500 acres (600 ha) reclaimed from the Yellow Sea off Incheon. 'Ubiquitous city' with ubiquitous sensing. Population 167,346 (2020).

markers.name: Masdar City, Abu Dhabi, UAE
markers.ctx: Zero-carbon planned city by Foster + Partners. Population ~5,000 vs 50,000 target. The smart city that couldn't attract residents.

markers.name: Quayside / Sidewalk Toronto, Canada
markers.ctx: Proposed 12-acre (4.9 ha) smart district at Quayside by Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs, after a 2017 Waterfront Toronto RFP. Drew sustained criticism over data collection. Alphabet withdrew on 7 May 2020, citing economic uncertainty from the COVID-19 pandemic.

markers.name: Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India
markers.ctx: New capital of Andhra Pradesh - 217 sq km, master plan by Foster + Partners. Land assembled by voluntary land pooling from 27 villages. Works halted after the 2019 change of government and resumed in June 2024; made the statutory capital by a 2026 amendment act.

markers.name: Nusantara, Borneo, Indonesia
markers.ctx: Designated new national capital replacing Jakarta, East Kalimantan; 256,000 hectares. Central government offices and palace built by 2024; transfer of civil servants planned from 2024 but phased.

markers.name: Forest City, Johor, Malaysia
markers.ctx: $100B development by Country Garden. Largely empty ghost city. The smart city that no one moved to.

markers.name: Microsoft HQ, Redmond, Washington
markers.ctx: Windows 72% desktops, Azure cloud, GitHub (100M+ developers), LinkedIn (1B users), VS Code, PowerShell. The operating system layer.

markers.name: Amazon / AWS HQ, Seattle
markers.ctx: Amazon / AWS: AWS held ~31% of cloud infrastructure (Synergy, Q1 2023). Ring doorbell camera network. Whole Foods. (The Washington Post is owned by Jeff Bezos personally, not by Amazon.) The infrastructure layer.

markers.name: Google / Alphabet HQ, Mountain View, CA
markers.ctx: Dominant in search, browsers (Chrome) and mobile OS (Android); YouTube 2B+ users (shares undated). Project Maven (Pentagon drone-imagery AI) - Google did not renew after 2018 staff protests. Project Nimbus: $1.2bn cloud contract, with Amazon, serving Israeli government agencies including the defence establishment.

markers.name: Meta HQ, Menlo Park, CA
markers.ctx: Zuckerberg: ~61% voting control (13.7% equity). Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp: 3bn+ users (undated company figure). Dual-class control concentrates the social graph's governance in one person.

markers.name: Menwith Hill, UK
markers.ctx: MoD-owned RAF station made available to the US DoD and run on behalf of the NSA; described as the largest electronic monitoring station in the world. Satellite ground station in dozens of radomes; alleged ECHELON site; connected to the national telecom network by BT fibre since 1992 (revealed in a 1997 court case). 2017: 1,205 staff incl. 344 US contractors and GCHQ personnel.

markers.name: Pine Gap, Northern Territory, Australia
markers.ctx: Joint Australia-US facility run by the Australian Signals Directorate with the CIA, NSA and NRO. Satellite ground station for US geostationary SIGINT satellites; attributed to the ECHELON network. Five Eyes southern-hemisphere SIGINT hub.

markers.name: Waihopai Station, New Zealand
markers.ctx: GCSB satellite-communications interception station in the Waihopai Valley near Blenheim; identified as part of ECHELON (attributed: MP Keith Locke, Nicky Hager). New Zealand's Five Eyes node.

markers.name: Misawa Air Base, Japan
markers.ctx: Misawa Security Operations Center, believed (attributed) to be one of the largest ECHELON ground stations. Five Eyes Asia-Pacific SIGINT node.

markers.name: Sugar Grove, West Virginia
markers.ctx: Former NSA radio/satellite intercept station run by the Navy; NSA relocated the mission and the base closed by 30 Sept 2015. Formerly cited as an ECHELON site.

markers.name: Yakima Research Station, Washington
markers.ctx: NSA satellite-intercept station (Yakima Research Station) inside the Yakima Training Center; cited as an ECHELON site. Reported in April 2013 to be closing, its function moving to Colorado.

markers.name: Gaza - Gaza Marine Gas Field
markers.ctx: Gaza Marine 1 and 2 gas fields, discovered September 2000 by British Gas under a Palestinian Authority licence, about 36 km offshore at ~610 m depth; estimated at over 1 trillion cubic feet; never developed.

markers.name: Wall Street / New Amsterdam, Manhattan
markers.ctx: Dutch West India Company settlement (1624-1664). Wall Street named after colony fortification wall. The financial capital sits on the extraction company's foundation.

markers.name: New Albany, Ohio
markers.ctx: Pop. ~409-414 (1980) → 10,825 (2020), roughly 2,500% growth. Built out by Les Wexner's investment from the 1990s; Maxwell told DOJ Epstein "ran New Albany" (attributed). Facebook data center. Google data center. Intel 926-acre fab plant.

markers.name: New Canaan, Connecticut
markers.ctx: Gold Coast. Median household income $141,788 (2000 Census). Philip Johnson Glass House. Harmony Lodge No. 67 (Masonic, 1763). Waveny Park: 300-acre former Texaco founder estate.

markers.name: Indian Creek Island, Florida
markers.ctx: 0.47 sq mi village, 41 home sites around the Indian Creek Country Club. One bridge to Surfside, guarded by a police checkpoint. 84 residents (2020 census). Residents include Jeff Bezos and Jared Kushner (a village council member); Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan bought a home here for a county-record $170 million (March 2026).

markers.name: Fisher Island, Florida
markers.ctx: 0.27 sq mi. No road or causeway: private ferry or yacht only, with pre-arranged security clearance. Bloomberg put average income at $2.5 million (2015), the highest of any US ZIP code. In 1963 an investment group led by Bebe Rebozo, including Richard Nixon and George Smathers, bought the Gar Wood estate here. 561 residents (2020).

markers.name: Library of Alexandria, Egypt
markers.ctx: One of the largest libraries of the ancient world. It declined gradually over centuries: damage in Caesar's fire (48 BC), the Brucheion quarter destroyed in the 270s and again in 297, the Serapeum daughter library destroyed in 391. The story that it was burned on Caliph Omar's order after the Arab conquest of 642 first appears in Arabic sources ~600 years later and is doubted by historians.

markers.name: House of Wisdom, Baghdad, Iraq
markers.ctx: Abbasid library and academy in Baghdad, destroyed in the Mongol siege of 1258. Chroniclers record that so many books were thrown into the Tigris that the river was said to run black with ink (chronicle account). No reliable count of its holdings exists.

markers.name: Nalanda University, Bihar, India
markers.ctx: Buddhist monastic university founded in the 5th century CE; likely attacked and ransacked by Bakhtiyar Khalji's forces c. 1200 CE. Its library's size is unknown - estimated in the hundreds of thousands of volumes; the popular 'nine million manuscripts' has no documentary source.

markers.name: Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt
markers.ctx: An estimated 2.3 million blocks (~6 million tonnes). Built c. 2560 BC. Sides aligned to the cardinal points within a few arcminutes; star-sighting methods that achieve this are documented in the Egyptological literature.

markers.name: Puma Punku, Tiwanaku, Bolivia
markers.ctx: Terraced platform mound of the Tiwanaku culture, built c. AD 536-600, faced with finely cut andesite and sandstone blocks - including the interlocking 'H-blocks' - joined with cast copper-arsenic-nickel cramps. ~3,850 m (12,600 ft) altitude. Claims of machine-precision tolerances and anachronistic technology come from ancient-astronaut literature and have no archaeological support.

markers.name: Baalbek, Lebanon
markers.ctx: Trilithon: three limestone blocks of ~800 t each, each over 19 m long, set in the Temple of Jupiter podium. In the nearby quarry lie the Stone of the Pregnant Woman (~1,000 t) and still larger unused blocks (~1,200 t and a block found in 2014). How Roman builders moved them is studied, not unexplained.

markers.name: Göbekli Tepe, Turkey
markers.ctx: Pre-Pottery Neolithic site occupied c. 9500-8000 BCE (~11,500 years ago), with large circular enclosures of carved T-shaped limestone pillars. Popularly called the 'world's first temple', but no definitive purpose has been established. Schmidt's early idea that it was deliberately backfilled has been revised: the enclosures repeatedly collapsed, were buried by landslides and were rebuilt.

markers.name: Monte Verde, Chile
markers.ctx: Pre-Clovis site near Puerto Montt. Monte Verde II, dated ~14,500 years ago and largely accepted, showed people were in South America at least ~1,000 years before Clovis and overturned the 'Clovis first' model after years of resistance. An older layer (MV-I, ~18,500 cal BP) remains contested.

markers.name: Visočica Hill (Bosnian Pyramid), Bosnia
markers.ctx: Natural hill promoted since 2005 by Semir Osmanagić as a 'Bosnian pyramid'. Direct study by geologists and archaeologists found the hills are natural flatiron formations with no sign of construction; the European Association of Archaeologists called the claim 'a cruel hoax'. Recorded as a killed specimen.

markers.name: Pine Ridge Reservation, South Dakota
markers.ctx: Oglala Lakota reservation. The North American pole of inaccessibility (the point farthest from any coast) lies within it, ~11 km north of Allen. Separately, the Black Hills (He Sapa), outside the reservation, were taken after the gold rush in breach of the 1868 treaty; Mount Rushmore was carved on the Lakota Six Grandfathers.

markers.name: Smithsonian Institution, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: Holds over 157 million items across 21 museums. Online claims that it suppresses 'giant skeleton' finds from 19th-century Bureau of Ethnology reports have no documentary support - unsupported.

markers.name: Eastern Congo / DRC - Cobalt Mines
markers.ctx: Children as young as 6 in artisanal cobalt mining. Cobalt → batteries → surveillance cameras → smart cities. The supply chain is built on child labor.

markers.name: Ukraine - Active Conflict Zone
markers.ctx: Russia-Ukraine war (full-scale invasion from 24 Feb 2022). Widely described as the largest land war in Europe since 1945. Major grain and energy infrastructure; Black Sea grain exports disrupted.

markers.name: Gaza - Active Conflict Zone
markers.ctx: Gaza-Israel war (from 7 Oct 2023). Mass civilian casualties, infrastructure destruction, forced displacement. MK-80 series bombs (US bodies made by General Dynamics) reported as the primary weapon type used. The Israeli government's Project Nimbus cloud contract (Google, Amazon) has military stakeholders, but no document shows it used for targeting. ICJ and ICC proceedings: see Section XV.

markers.name: Sudan - Active Conflict Zone
markers.ctx: Civil war since 15 April 2023, SAF vs RSF. Over 10 million displaced (UN agencies; peak estimates higher). Ethnic violence in Darfur. Significant gold reserves; gold moves largely through Dubai. Arms supply: OFAC designations name UAE-based companies; the Emirati state role is attributed, not documented (see Section XV).

markers.name: Myanmar - Active Conflict Zone
markers.ctx: Civil War (Feb 2021-present). Military junta. Airstrikes against civilians. Millions displaced. Rare earth mineral supply chain.

markers.name: Darfur, Sudan
markers.ctx: Darfur region within the Sudan war: RSF siege and capture of El Fasher (Oct 2025) and mass killings in West Darfur (Masalit). Gold mining areas lie within the conflict zone; a causal link is not established here.

markers.name: Pentagon, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: Operation Northwoods: on 13 March 1962 the Joint Chiefs of Staff submitted to Defense Secretary McNamara proposals for false-flag acts - including staged attacks at Guantanamo, sinking refugee boats and terrorism in US cities - to justify an invasion of Cuba. The proposals were rejected by President Kennedy.

markers.name: Gulf of Tonkin, Vietnam - DESOTO patrol area
markers.ctx: 2-4 Aug 1964. FOIA-SOURCED UPGRADE (read directly from NSA's reading room, 18 Aug 2026). NSA released its Tonkin holdings in two tranches - 30 Nov 2005 and 30 May 2006 - and states on the release page that it was 'not NSA's intention to prove or disprove any one set of conclusions,' only to publish the material. The substantive finding is NSA historian Robert J. Hanyok's Cryptologic Quarterly study 'Skunks, Bogies, Silent Hounds, and the Flying Fish: The Gulf of Tonkin Mystery, 2-4 August 1964' (classified 2001, declassified Nov 2005): the 2 Aug attack happened; the 4 Aug attack did not; and the SIGINT product that appeared to confirm it was built from 4 Aug intercepts about recovery of the P-4s damaged on 2 Aug - re-dated, re-translated and selectively excerpted. PRECISION: that is Hanyok's conclusion, not an institutional NSA finding, and he describes a mix of analytic error and deliberate misrepresentation rather than a single fabrication order. Collection also holds CAPT J.J. Herrick, Col Ralph Steakley (DESOTO) and Lt Col Delmar C. Lang reports. Sources: nsa.gov Gulf of Tonkin release; rel1_skunks_bogies.pdf.

markers.name: Fort Benning (Fort Moore 2023-25) - School of the Americas / WHINSEC
markers.ctx: School of the Americas (here since 1984), renamed WHINSEC by the 2001 NDAA. Alumni include dictators Noriega, Galtieri, Banzer and Rios Montt (genocide conviction 2013, overturned 10 days later) and death-squad leader Roberto D Aubuisson. The report reads the rename as continuity under a new name.

markers.name: Carlisle Barracks, PA - U.S. Army War College
markers.ctx: U.S. Army War College. Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, class of 2006, became Egypt's Director of Military Intelligence in Jan 2010, led the July 2013 removal of President Morsi, and as president is building the New Administrative Capital (714 km2 planned).

markers.name: National Defense University, Washington D.C.
markers.ctx: International officers program trains foreign military leaders in U.S. doctrine. Graduates return carrying the architecture in their training.

markers.name: Fort Leavenworth, KS - Command and General Staff College
markers.ctx: International Military Student program. Foreign officers trained in U.S. command philosophy and strategic doctrine.

markers.name: Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, UK
markers.ctx: Trained King Abdullah II (Jordan), Sultan Qaboos (Oman) and Crown Prince Hussein of Jordan (2017); King Hamad of Bahrain passed out of Mons Officer Cadet School (1968), later merged into Sandhurst. The empire ended; the officer pipeline did not.

markers.name: Tehran, Iran - 1953 Operation Ajax
markers.ctx: 19 Aug 1953: CIA-MI6 operation removed Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh and strengthened the Shah; the U.S. has since officially acknowledged its role. CIA helped establish and train SAVAK (Mossad role attributed). The report reads 1979 as blowback.

markers.name: Guatemala City - 1954 Operation PBSUCCESS
markers.ctx: 18-27 June 1954: CIA operation authorised by Eisenhower removed elected President Jacobo Arbenz. Secretary of State John Foster Dulles and CIA Director Allen Dulles both had significant prior links to the United Fruit Company.

markers.name: Kinshasa, Congo - 1961 Lumumba Assassination
markers.ctx: Patrice Lumumba, Congo's first prime minister, was executed 17 Jan 1961 near Elisabethville, Katanga, by Katangan authorities with Belgian participation; Belgium admitted moral responsibility in 2002. Eisenhower had authorised a CIA poisoning plan in 1960 that was not carried out. Mobutu ruled 1965-1997; estimates of his wealth run up to $5 billion.

markers.name: Jakarta, Indonesia - 1965 lists of names
markers.ctx: 1965-66: the army destroyed the PKI and Suharto displaced Sukarno, ruling until 1998. The U.S. Embassy supplied the army with lists of up to 5,000 suspected communists (CIA role attributed). 500,000 to 1,000,000+ killed.

markers.name: Santiago, Chile - 1973 Allende Coup
markers.ctx: 11 Sept 1973: Allende died in La Moneda during the coup. The Church Committee study Covert Action in Chile 1963-1973 documented CIA funding of the opposition (about $8 million, 1970-73; figure attributed). Under Pinochet about 3,000 people were killed or disappeared.

markers.name: Congress for Cultural Freedom HQ, Paris
markers.ctx: Founded 26 June 1950 in West Berlin, headquartered in Paris; CIA-funded until 1966. At its height active in 35 countries with 20+ magazines, exhibitions and conferences. CIA funding exposed 1966-67 (New York Times, then Ramparts).

markers.name: Fort Belvoir, VA - ISA / Task Force Orange HQ
markers.ctx: Intelligence Support Activity headquarters. JSOC field-intelligence unit, created 1981 from the Field Operations Group formed in 1980 after Eagle Claw. Nicknamed The Activity and the Army of Northern Virginia; has used a dozen two-word SAP names (CENTRA SPIKE, GRAY FOX, CEMETERY WIND...). Provides SIGINT/HUMINT to JSOC units.

markers.name: Arlington, VA - ISA First Secret HQ
markers.ctx: The ISA was given a classified budget of $7 million, a secret headquarters in Arlington and the cover name Tactical Concept Activity (1981); its records sat under the SAP OPTIMIZE TALENT. Exact site not public.

markers.name: Tegucigalpa, Honduras - SEASPRAY/ISA Operations Base
markers.ctx: Operation Queens Hunter (early 1980s): ISA SIGINT specialists flying in SEASPRAY Beechcraft King Airs based in Honduras monitored Salvadoran guerrilla communications. In the same theatre, SOA-trained officers led death squads (attributed); the report reads this as one government funding both.

markers.name: Medellín, Colombia - CENTRA SPIKE / Pablo Escobar Hunt
markers.ctx: ISA SIGINT team CENTRA SPIKE tracked Pablo Escobar's communications (1989-93) in support of Colombia's Search Bloc, which killed him in Medellin on 2 Dec 1993 (Mark Bowden, Killing Pablo; attributed).

markers.name: Mount Waterman, Angeles National Forest, CA - Reza LKP
markers.ctx: Monica Jacinto Reza - Mondaloy alloy co-inventor (US Patent 2010/0266442 A1), Columbia BS, UCLA MS, Aerojet Rocketdyne Technical Fellow, then JPL. Last known position June 22 2025. FLIR-negative (no thermal signature). Scent trail terminated. Find a Grave memorial created 4 days later - 'green burial' designation while SAR still active.

markers.name: Sandia Mountains, Albuquerque, NM - McCasland Disappearance
markers.ctx: Maj. Gen. William Neil McCasland - AFRL Commander 2011-2013, oversaw AFRL's R&D portfolio, which included the Mondaloy qualification work (attributed). Vanished hiking February 27 2026. Left all electronics behind. Named in Tom DeLonge's 25 Jan 2016 email to John Podesta (WikiLeaks Podesta emailid 3099). Whether his disappearance relates to his career is not established.

markers.name: Wright-Patterson AFB, Dayton, OH - AFRL HQ
markers.ctx: Air Force Research Laboratory headquarters. Dallis Hardwick - first Mondaloy co-inventor - served at AFRL Materials and Manufacturing Directorate. Died 5 Jan 2014 of metastatic breast cancer (UNSW). Of the three people the report groups around the alloy, one died of documented illness and two are missing; no link between the cases is established.

markers.name: JPL / La Cañada Flintridge, CA - Reza's Employer
markers.ctx: Jet Propulsion Laboratory - Reza's employer at time of disappearance. JPL issued no public statement. NASA headquarters silent. Aerojet Rocketdyne (former employer) silent. AIAA silent. SpaceNews silent. Employers and trade press routinely decline comment on open missing-person cases; the silence is logged, not read.

markers.name: Mena, Arkansas - CIA Cocaine Transshipment
markers.ctx: Barry Seal's base of operations. Seal, a Medellin cartel smuggler turned DEA informant, based aircraft at Mena's Intermountain airport; a 2020-released FBI/State Police/IRS document records smuggling activity there 1980-84. CIA ties are alleged, not documented. Murdered by cartel gunmen in Baton Rouge, 19 Feb 1986. State Police investigator Russell Welch said he was later infected with anthrax (his account).

markers.name: Ilopango Air Base, El Salvador
markers.ctx: Base of the Contra arms-resupply network (documented); allegations that return flights carried cocaine come from DEA agent Celerino Castillo (attributed). Oliver North's notebooks reference the operation. Kerry Committee (13 Apr 1989): "substantial evidence of drug smuggling" by individual Contras, their suppliers and pilots, and State Department payments to traffickers - not a finding of policy.

markers.name: Culiacán, Sinaloa, Mexico - Cartel HQ
markers.ctx: Sinaloa Cartel headquarters. Jesús Vicente Zambada-Niebla claimed in 2011 court filings that the cartel had an immunity-for-intelligence agreement with DEA; DEA denied it (claim, not established). El Chapo escaped twice (2001, 2015) - the 2015 Altiplano escape ran through a mile-long tunnel with a motorcycle on rails, GPS-tracked to within inches of his cell. The tunnels reach into maximum-security prisons, not just across the border.

markers.name: Otay Mesa, California - Cartel Tunnel
markers.ctx: Major tunnel corridor between Tijuana and San Diego; the longest found on the Southwest border (4,309 ft, with rail, ventilation and an elevator) ended in an Otay Mesa warehouse district (announced Jan 2020). Sinaloa Cartel operated sophisticated drug tunnels with rail systems, ventilation, and electricity. Distribution hub connecting Mexican production to U.S. market.

markers.name: Chicago, Illinois - Sinaloa Distribution Hub
markers.ctx: DEA identified Chicago as the primary Sinaloa Cartel distribution hub in the United States. The cartel used Chicago as a central node to supply cocaine, heroin, and methamphetamine to the entire eastern seaboard and Midwest.

markers.name: Arezzo, Italy - P2 Lodge / Villa Wanda
markers.ctx: Licio Gelli's Villa Wanda - headquarters of Propaganda Due (P2) Masonic lodge. 962 members including 44 parliamentarians, military commanders, intelligence chiefs, financiers, media editors. Gelli's 'Plan of Democratic Rebirth' - a 53-point manifesto for authoritarian capture of Italian democracy through media control, judicial infiltration, and constitutional amendment.

markers.name: Milan, Italy - Banco Ambrosiano
markers.ctx: Banco Ambrosiano headquarters. Italy's largest private bank collapsed in 1982 with a $1.287 billion hole. Chairman Roberto Calvi found hanged under Blackfriars Bridge, London. Vatican Bank (IOR) was the principal shareholder. Calvi was a member of Gelli's P2 lodge.

markers.name: Blackfriars Bridge, London - Calvi Murder
markers.ctx: Roberto Calvi - 'God's Banker' - found hanging under Blackfriars Bridge, June 18, 1982. Pockets filled with bricks and cash. First inquest: suicide (1982); second: open verdict (1983); a 2002 forensic report found murder, police reopened it as murder (2003), and a Rome court (2007) found murder but acquitted all five accused.

markers.name: Reggio Calabria, Italy - 'Ndrangheta HQ
markers.ctx: 'Ndrangheta homeland. Estimated revenue €44-53 billion/year - 3% of Italian GDP. Italian investigators have estimated 80% of Europe's cocaine transits Gioia Tauro under its control; EMCDDA/Europol name Iberia as the primary entry point. Decentralized 'ndrine (family clans) make it nearly impossible to dismantle. Global operations in 30+ countries.

markers.name: Gioia Tauro, Italy - 'Ndrangheta Port
markers.ctx: Calabrian port infiltrated by the 'Ndrangheta. Primary cocaine entry point for European distribution. Italy's largest container port (6th in the Mediterranean), used as a logistics hub for narcotics trafficking.

markers.name: San Luca, Italy - 'Ndrangheta Origin
markers.ctx: Spiritual and organizational homeland of the 'Ndrangheta. Annual pilgrimage to the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Polsi serves as the organization's annual meeting for strategic decisions. Duisburg massacre (2007) - six 'Ndrangheta members killed in Germany - originated from a San Luca clan feud.

markers.name: Duisburg, Germany - 'Ndrangheta Massacre
markers.ctx: August 15, 2007: six Italian men aged 16-38, tied to one side of the San Luca feud, shot dead outside Da Bruno restaurant. The massacre exposed 'Ndrangheta's deep presence in Germany and broader European operations. Led to increased European law enforcement focus on Calabrian organized crime.

markers.name: Rotterdam, Netherlands - Cocaine Port
markers.ctx: Europe's largest port. Primary 'Ndrangheta cocaine entry point for Northern Europe. Seizures fell from 45.5 tons (2023) to 25.9 tons (2024); authorities have estimated they intercept only a fraction of the flow (attributed).

markers.name: Antwerp, Belgium - Cocaine Port
markers.ctx: Europe's second-largest port. Massive cocaine transshipment hub, often exceeding Rotterdam in seizure volumes. 'Ndrangheta and Albanian organized crime networks coordinate distribution through the port.

markers.name: HSBC HQ, London - Cartel Laundering
markers.ctx: HSBC fined $1.9 billion (2012) for laundering $881 million for Sinaloa and Norte del Valle cartels. Its US arm failed to monitor more than $670 billion in wire transfers from HSBC Mexico. No criminal charges against any individual. The fine was reported as roughly five weeks of profit (press estimate).

markers.name: Luxembourg - BCCI
markers.ctx: BCCI (Bank of Credit and Commerce International), registered in Luxembourg - shut down in 1991 for massive fraud and laundering. The CIA held several accounts there and in 1991 admitted it knew of its drug laundering. Laundered for Medellín Cartel, Noriega, Abu Nidal, and nuclear proliferation networks. Founded 1972, collapsed 1991.

markers.name: São Paulo, Brazil - PCC-'Ndrangheta Nexus
markers.ctx: Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) alliance with 'Ndrangheta - cocaine flows from Andean production through Brazilian ports to Calabrian distribution networks in Europe. São Paulo serves as the logistics and financial coordination hub.

markers.name: Bologna, Italy - Strategy of Tension
markers.ctx: August 2, 1980: Bologna train station bombing - 85 dead, 200+ wounded. NAR neo-fascists convicted; 2020s Bologna proceedings named P2 head Licio Gelli among the instigators. Vincenzo Vinciguerra (neo-fascist, serving life for the 1972 Peteano bombing) testified that NATO stay-behind networks organized false flag attacks to blame the left and justify authoritarian state responses.

markers.name: Managua, Nicaragua - Dual-Funding
markers.ctx: Banco Ambrosiano funded both the Somoza dictatorship and its Sandinista opposition - the same bank on both sides. Separately, an Ambrosiano subsidiary financed an attempted Exocet purchase for Argentina during the Falklands War; no link between the two is documented.

markers.name: Medellín, Colombia - CENTRA SPIKE / ISA
markers.ctx: ISA (Intelligence Support Activity) operation CENTRA SPIKE tracked Pablo Escobar using signals intelligence.

markers.name: Necker Island, BVI (Richard Branson)
markers.ctx: 74 acres. Richard Branson saw it in 1978 and bought it about a year later from Lord Cobham for $180,000. Run as a Virgin Limited Edition resort. Barack and Michelle Obama visited as Branson's guests (Feb 2017). The Great House burned down after a lightning strike in Aug 2011; Hurricane Irma devastated the island in Sept 2017.

markers.name: Moskito Island, BVI (Branson)
markers.ctx: 125 acres on the west side of Gorda Sound, bought by Richard Branson in 2007 for GBP 10 million; near his Necker Island. Barack Obama learned to kiteboard here in February 2017. Two private islands, one jurisdiction, one owner.

markers.name: Skorpios, Greece (Onassis → Rybolovleva lease)
markers.ctx: About 206 acres (83.2 ha). Bought in 1963 by Aristotle Onassis, who married Jacqueline Kennedy here on 20 October 1968. In April 2013 Ekaterina Rybolovleva, daughter of Russian potash billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev, bought companies from Athina Onassis's trust for $153 million, including a long-term lease of the island. Shipping dynasty to Russian potash fortune.

markers.name: Tetiaroa, French Polynesia (Brando)
markers.ctx: 12 motu, about 585 ha (1,450 acres) of land. The Tahitian royal family sold the atoll to dentist Johnston Walter Williams in 1904; Marlon Brando bought the motu from a Williams descendant in the late 1960s. Now The Brando resort, on islets held under a 99-year lease signed by Brando.

markers.name: Lanai, Hawaii (Larry Ellison)
markers.ctx: About 98% of the island, bought in June 2012 from Castle & Cooke for $300 million by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison; the rest is state land or individually owned homes. Population 3,367 (2020).

markers.name: Musha Cay, Bahamas (David Copperfield)
markers.ctx: Privately owned island of about 700 acres in the Exuma Cays, 85 miles southeast of Nassau, owned by illusionist David Copperfield and let to one group of guests at a time.

markers.name: Peter Island, BVI (Van Andel family)
markers.ctx: 1,800 acres, the largest private island in the BVI. Owned by the Amway Corporation from 1978 until 2001, when full ownership passed to the Van Andel family, one of Amway's two founding families (the other is DeVos).
